title.narrative: Indicator 2.1. Number of governments, standardsetters or financial institutions that consider adopting and/or implement AML legislation, policies and standards based on TI recommendations.

description.narrative: Measures the extent to which various governmental entities are influenced by the recommendations provided by Transparency International (TI) in their efforts to combat money laundering (AML) and transnational corruption. Specifically, it tracks:Governments: National governments or regional bodies that review, adopt, or enforce AMLrelated laws and regulations.StandardSetters: Organizations or bodies that establish norms and guidelines for AML practices, such as financial regulatory authorities or international standards organizations.Financial Institutions: Banks, credit unions, insurance companies, and other financial entities that incorporate TIs AML recommendations into their internal policies and operational procedures.Adopting: The indicator includes entities that are in the process of evaluating or planning to integrate TIs AML recommendations.Implement: It also covers entities that have already put these recommendations into practice through formal adoption of legislation, policies, or standards.TI Recommendations: Refers to the specific guidance and best practices proposed by Transparency International aimed at strengthening AML frameworks and reducing the risk of money laundering activities.

description.narrative: This indicator measures the quantity of actionable, researchbacked recommendations that are formally presented to key stakeholders, including governments, financial authorities, and international financial institutions. These recommendations are specifically designed to address issues of crossborder corruption and prevent budgetary and fiscal leakages, which are significant factors contributing to economic inequalities.EvidenceBased Recommendations: Suggestions and proposals that are grounded in rigorous research and data analysis, ensuring their credibility and effectiveness.Presented to Stakeholders: The target audience includes:Governments: National and regional governments that can implement policies and regulations.Financial Authorities: Regulatory bodies that oversee financial institutions and markets.International Financial Institutions: Organisations such as the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank that play a role in global financial stability and development.Combating CrossBorder Corruption: Efforts aimed at preventing and addressing corruption that transcends national borders, which often involves complex financial networks and regulatory challenges.Stopping Budgetary/Fiscal Leakages: Identifying and eliminating inefficiencies and illicit flows of public funds that undermine economic stability and equitable resource distribution.Impact on Inequalities: The ultimate goal of these recommendations is to reduce economic disparities by ensuring fair and effective use of public resources.

title.narrative: Indicator 1.3.1. Number of knowledge products of public opinion based on surveys and studies on social values, attitudes, beliefs and opinion towards corruption, inequality, and fiscal justice.

description.narrative: Knowledge products are the outcomes or results of research endeavors, such as reports, articles, or data sets, that disseminate the knowledge gained from surveys and studies.Public opinion pertains to the collective views, thoughts, and sentiments held by individuals within a particular society or community.Surveys and studies refer to research activities conducted to collect data and information from a representative sample of the population to understand their attitudes and beliefs.Social values, attitudes, beliefs, and opinions encompass the individuals perspectives, values, judgments, and viewpoints on various social, political, and economic matters.Corruption refers to the abuse of power, position, or resources for personal gain or to serve the interests of a few at the expense of the broader public.Inequality relates to the disparities in wealth, income, opportunities, or access to resources among individuals or social groups.Fiscal justice concerns fair and equitable taxation and government expenditure policies aimed at addressing social and economic imbalances.

title.narrative: Indicator 1.3.3. Number of multistakeholder platforms, round tables of spaces on the convergence of corruption, human rights, fiscal justice, and inequality in public opinion.

description.narrative: Multistakeholder platforms are forums or spaces that involve the participation and collaboration of various stakeholders from different sectors, backgrounds, or perspectives.Round tables are organized discussions or meetings in which participants exchange views and engage in constructive dialogue on specific topics.Spaces refer to venues or platforms, whether physical or virtual, where people can come together to interact and share ideas.Convergence in this context refers to the point at which issues related to corruption, human rights, fiscal justice, and inequality intersect or overlap.Corruption refers to the misuse of power, position, or resources for personal gain or to serve the interests of a few at the expense of the broader public.Human rights encompass the basic rights and freedoms to which all individuals are entitled, irrespective of their background or characteristics.Fiscal justice concerns fair and equitable taxation and government expenditure policies aimed at addressing social and economic imbalances.

comment.narrative: Target value indicates at least 6 multistakeholder spaces.

description.narrative: Behavioral sciences interventions are actions, programs, or strategies based on research and theories from behavioral sciences (such as psychology, sociology, or economics) that aim to influence or modify human behavior to achieve desired outcomes.Public opinion analysis involves studying and understanding the perspectives, attitudes, and beliefs of the general public on specific issues or topics through surveys, polls, or other research methods.Civic participation refers to the involvement of individuals in decisionmaking processes, community activities, or public affairs, typically in the context of governance and societal development.Social inclusion relates to ensuring that all individuals have equal opportunities, access to resources, and participation in social, economic, and political activities, regardless of their background or characteristics.

title.narrative: Indicator 1.3.4. Percentage of designed, developed, or implemented tools and interventions that incorporate gender equality and social inclusion criteria or public opinion knowledge.

description.narrative: Designed, developed, or implemented tools and interventions refer to various measures, programs, policies, or resources that have been planned, created, or put into practice to address specific issues or achieve certain goals.Gender equality pertains to the fair and equal treatment of individuals of all genders, ensuring that women, men, and genderdiverse individuals have the same opportunities, rights, and access to resources and decisionmaking processes.Social inclusion involves ensuring that all individuals, regardless of their background, race, ethnicity, religion, disability, or other characteristics, have equal access to opportunities, services, and participation in society.Public opinion knowledge relates to insights gained from analysing the perspectives, attitudes, and beliefs of the general public on various topics through surveys, polls, or other research methods.
